obvious: A small set of private funds (8VC, Founders Fund, In-Q-Tel, Lux, Silent Ventures, Valor, Washington Harbour, a16z American Dynamism) hold the same few companies: Anduril sits in 8 of the 11 funds the repo censused and Hadrian and Impulse in 5 each; a broad retail fund (Fundrise) holds Anduril, SpaceX and Erebor as well, so overlap alone is also what an ordinary diversified mandate looks like.

Those companies are then rated by a ranking whose 2026 entry rule is a US government contract, whose scoring partners are investment firms (Franklin Templeton, Balyasny), whose co-founder is also a co-head at one of them, and whose weights, candidate pool, rejected rows and FOCI decisions are unpublished with no appeal route; Anduril was #2, #2, #1, #1 across 2023 to 2026, and Silent Ventures' own list overlaps it on 11 of 23 censused companies.

Public money then enters at the gates the credential points toward: a DPA Title III award on a stated $75M private match (2025-01-07), an NGC2 prototype OTA (2025-07-18) followed by the data-baseline lead role (2026-06-22), a $20B-ceiling single-award Army enterprise IDIQ (2026-03-13), and a $362.97M CBP order (2025-12-25) that came after (temporal sequence only) a $700,000 lobbying quarter naming the same program and a statute limiting funds to towers CBP had already accepted; Palantir's equivalent is a sole-source $10B-ceiling enterprise agreement and 54% government revenue ($2.402B in FY2025).

Capital, credential, contract and next round form a loop in which every link is public and individually documented (the repo alleges no wrongdoing), no link requires the others to coordinate, and the external checks the record shows act at the contract gate, where GAO, courts and competitors operate (Palantir beat the Army in court on DCGS-A2; Anduril lost a GAO protest and had a Phase III solicitation cancelled; the Marines drew ten offers).

People move across the seam in both directions and each move is individually visible in the record: Kausner (State/Senate/DIU/Navy to Anduril, 2022), Obadal (Anduril to Under Secretary of the Army, 2025-09-22), Sankar of Palantir into an Army Reserve advisory unit (2025-06-13), Warner and Cooper (No. 10 and DHSC to Electric Twin, 2023), Case (Cabinet Secretary to Barrow chair to Electric Twin ethics board, 2025 to 2026), Donnelly and DeMartino (OSD/CENTCOM to Pallas); where an ethics regime is documented (UK Business Appointment Rules for Case) it binds future conduct rather than recording observed conduct, and for the US moves (Kausner, Obadal) no ethics file is public.

Clifford's documented roles are all advisory, convening or unpaid (summit representative, Taskforce board vice-chair, ARIA chair, unpaid AI Opportunities Adviser) and none carries award or source-selection authority, so the record contains no contract, payment or decision he signed; the one private-interest overlap on file (Faculty shares, declared 2024-10-10, divested by 2025-02-24) is handled by a register plus a divest-by-date, not a decision-level recusal log.

The Action Plan he led recommends the demand-side machinery (government as strategic AI customer, procurement reform, sovereign compute, domestic champions, national-security collaboration), was accepted in full on 2025-01-13, and on the same day he was appointed unpaid adviser on its implementation; the supplier side (Anduril UK, Palantir in the NHS and Homes for Ukraine, Faculty, Electric Twin) is documented in other records, and no instrument joins the two sides.

Anduril UK's own documented path runs through ministers and MoD rather than through Clifford: six instruments from 2021 to 2025 with stated values of roughly GBP 78M (375k, 3.7M, 21.1M, 6.3M, 17M and about 30M), at least three of them single-source or negotiated without prior publication, a Defence Secretary visit to Anduril in Washington the day before the 6 March 2025 deal, a DBT meeting on 19 May 2025, a Chequers lunch, Atlantic Bastion, DDAD and the Project NYX downselect; the repo's closed result is that Clifford and Anduril share a policy ecology and one Summit-window overlap, with no two-sided instrument.

The same few names recur on both sides of the Atlantic without a connecting document: Anduril (UK supplier and US portfolio holding), Palantir (Louis Mosley on the same 2 June 2023 roundtable list as Clifford, and as an Electric Twin angel in 2026), a16z-adjacent capital (Boyle's board seats; Andreessen as an Electric Twin angel), and Dialog (Thiel co-founder; Clifford, Lonsdale, Army Secretary Driscoll and five of the Entrepreneur First investors and advisers named in the raw master are on the directory).

The decisive joints sit in artifacts nobody is required to publish and the record names them: appointment memoranda and candidate lists, recommendation redlines, source-selection and J&A files, ethics and recusal files, ranking weights and rejected rows, allotment schedules and side letters, closing documents for conditional commitments.

Unpaid, part-time or 'individual capacity' roles (Case on Electric Twin's ethics board, Detachment 201 officers, Clifford as adviser, Muthukrishna as adviser to the company whose accuracy article credits 'independent validation' to his institution, Moses's self-described advisories) place people between public and private actors without leaving a payroll, contract or filing trail, so for this kind of role the record that would prove or disprove influence is of a type that is not generated or not published, not merely one nobody has found.

Conditional and ceiling instruments carry the headline while the money is unobserved: four of five named OSC instruments are conditional with none closed, Erebor was charter-approved on conditions that include an equity line whose terms are unpublished, and the Army enterprise vehicles are ceilings, not obligations (Anduril's CBP order shows $362.97M obligated against $24.5M outlaid).

What the record does not contain is equally structural: no document links Jackson Moses or Silent Ventures to Clifford, the MoD, Faculty or Electric Twin, and the only shared node is Anduril itself (a self-listed prior Silent investment and a UK MoD supplier); no Clifford-Palantir or Clifford-Thiel instrument exists beyond co-presence and a listing; and the repo's own gates treat dense co-listing as non-adjacency, so a reader gets the shared incentives and the missing join side by side, which is the repo's stated method rather than a verdict.
